parts.text: M forms M²⁺ ions. Write an ionic equation for the reaction of M with copper(II) ions.
parts.answer: M + Cu²⁺ → M²⁺ + Cu

parts.label: c
parts.text: Plan an experiment using temperature changes to check whether M is more reactive than iron. Give the measurements and how you would decide.
parts.answer: Add equal masses of powdered M and powdered iron separately to equal volumes of the same copper(II) sulfate solution in an insulated cup; measure the starting and highest temperatures; the metal giving the larger temperature rise is more reactive.
parts.working: B1 same mass/particle size and volume/concentration of CuSO₄; B1 measure initial and maximum temperature; B1 larger rise = more reactive.

author: HomiLabs

stem:
A student sets up four test tubes, each containing an iron nail, and leaves them for one week.
A: nail in tap water, open to the air
B: nail in boiled water with a layer of oil on top
C: nail in dry air with anhydrous calcium chloride, tube stoppered
D: nail in salt water, open to the air

parts.label: a
parts.text: In which tubes does the nail rust?
parts.answer: A and D

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the purpose of boiling the water and adding a layer of oil in tube B.
parts.answer: Boiling removes dissolved air (oxygen); the oil stops air dissolving back into the water.

parts.label: c
parts.text: What do the results show is needed for iron to rust?
parts.answer: Both water and oxygen (air).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest which tube rusts fastest and why.
parts.answer: D: salt water speeds up rusting.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which method protects a steel ship's hull by sacrificial protection?
A painting the hull
B coating the hull with oil
C attaching blocks of zinc to the hull
D covering the hull with plastic
parts.answer: C attaching blocks of zinc to the hull
parts.working: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes instead of the steel. A, B and D are barrier methods and stop protecting if the coating is damaged.

stem: Galvanised steel sheets are widely used for roofs of sheds and cattle shelters in rural Punjab.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by galvanising.
parts.answer: Coating iron or steel with a layer of zinc.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A galvanised steel roof sheet is scratched, exposing the steel. Explain why the steel still does not rust.
parts.answer: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so zinc loses electrons (is oxidised) in preference to iron. The zinc corrodes instead of the iron (sacrificial protection).
parts.working: B1 zinc more reactive; B1 zinc oxidised / loses electrons instead of iron; B1 iron protected even where exposed.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why a painted steel gate starts to rust when the paint is chipped.
parts.answer: Paint is only a barrier; once broken, water and oxygen reach the iron.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the chemical name of rust and write a word equation for its formation.
parts.answer: hydrated iron(III) oxide; iron + water + oxygen → hydrated iron(III) oxide

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest why cars in Karachi rust faster than cars in a dry inland city.
parts.answer: Karachi is coastal: the air is humid and contains salt, and salt (an electrolyte) speeds up rusting.
parts.working: B1 more moisture; B1 salt speeds up rusting.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give two barrier methods for preventing rusting of a bicycle and say which part each is used for.
parts.answer: Paint for the frame; oil or grease for the chain; plastic coating for the basket / handlebars.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any two matched methods.

stem: A student pushes damp iron wool into the bottom of a measuring cylinder and turns it upside down in a trough of water. The volume of air trapped is 100.0 cm³ at the start. After eight days, when the reading has stopped changing, the volume is 79.2 cm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the percentage of the air used up.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the gas that was used up and explain why the water level rose.
parts.answer: Oxygen; it reacted with the iron to form rust, so the volume of gas fell and water moved up to take its place.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why the student waited until the reading stopped changing.
parts.answer: To make sure all the oxygen had reacted.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest one source of error and one improvement.
parts.answer: Error: temperature or pressure changes alter the gas volume; reading not at eye level / meniscus. Improvement: keep at constant temperature and read at the same temperature; use more iron wool (or wet it) so all the oxygen reacts; repeat and average.

author: HomiLabs

stem: Sialkot is known for making surgical instruments and cutlery from stainless steel.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by an alloy.
parts.answer: A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements (usually metals).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the two metals in brass.
parts.answer: copper and zinc

parts.label: c
parts.text: Stainless steel contains iron, chromium and nickel. Give one use of stainless steel and the property that makes it suitable.
parts.answer: Cutlery / kitchen sinks / surgical instruments; it is hard and resists rusting.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Why is an alloy usually harder than the pure metal it is made from?
A Atoms of different sizes disrupt the regular layers, so the layers cannot slide easily.
B The alloy contains covalent bonds between the atoms.
C The alloy has no delocalised electrons.
D The atoms in an alloy are all the same size and packed more tightly.
parts.answer: A Atoms of different sizes disrupt the regular layers, so the layers cannot slide easily.
parts.working: Different-sized atoms distort the layers, making it harder for layers to slide. B and C are wrong: alloys still have metallic bonding with delocalised electrons.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain, in terms of structure, why brass is harder than pure copper. You may describe a diagram in words.
parts.answer: In pure copper the atoms are all the same size and arranged in regular layers that slide easily. In brass the zinc atoms are a different size; they distort the layers so the layers cannot slide over each other easily, so brass is harder.
parts.working: B1 pure metal: regular layers slide easily; B1 alloy: atoms of different sizes disrupt layers; B1 layers cannot slide easily → harder.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Brass is used for door handles and musical instruments. Give one reason, other than hardness, why brass is used rather than iron.
parts.answer: It does not rust / resists corrosion; attractive gold colour.

stem:
A metallurgist measures the hardness of copper–zinc alloys (higher number = harder).
% zinc: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40
hardness: 40, 52, 63, 75, 86

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how the hardness changes as the percentage of zinc increases.
parts.answer: Hardness increases as the percentage of zinc increases (by about 11–12 units per 10 % zinc).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Estimate the hardness of an alloy containing 25 % zinc.
parts.answer: 69 (accept 68–70)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why an alloy with 30 % zinc is better than pure copper for making screws and hinges.
parts.answer: It is much harder (75 vs 40) so it is stronger and less easily bent or worn, while still resisting corrosion.
parts.working: B1 harder / stronger; B1 data quoted.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: A 250 g sample of brass contains 64 % copper by mass. Calculate the masses of copper and zinc in the sample.
parts.answer: copper 160 g; zinc 90 g

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the ratio of copper atoms to zinc atoms. Give your answer as x : 1 to 3 significant figures. (Ar: Cu = 64, Zn = 65)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why brass is described as a mixture and not a compound.
parts.answer: The metals are not chemically combined in a fixed ratio; the composition of brass can vary (and it keeps the metallic properties of its components).
parts.working: B1 not chemically bonded / no fixed formula; B1 variable composition.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which compound is in the same homologous series as ethanol?
A C₃H₇OH
B CH₃COOH
C C₃H₆
D C₂H₆
parts.answer: A C₃H₇OH
parts.working: C₃H₇OH (propanol) has the same –OH functional group and general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH. CH₃COOH (B) is a carboxylic acid, a different series.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give three characteristics of a homologous series.
parts.answer: Same general formula; same functional group; similar chemical properties; a trend in physical properties (e.g. boiling point increases with chain length); each member differs from the next by CH₂.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The general formula of the alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Write the molecular formula of the alkane with 8 carbon atoms, found in petrol.
parts.answer: C₈H₁₈

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the general formula of the alkenes.
parts.answer: CₙH₂ₙ

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by structural isomers.
parts.answer: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.
parts.working: B1 same molecular formula; B1 different structures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the structural formulae of the two structural isomers with the molecular formula C₄H₁₀.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (butane) and CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃ (methylpropane)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the structural formulae of but-1-ene and but-2-ene.
parts.answer: but-1-ene: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃; but-2-ene: CH₃CH=CHCH₃

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name each compound:
(i) CH₃CH₂COOH
(ii) CH₃CH₂CH₂OH
(iii) CH₃CH=CH₂
(iv) CH₃COOCH₂CH₃
parts.answer: (i) propanoic acid (ii) propan-1-ol (iii) propene (iv) ethyl ethanoate

parts.label: b
parts.text: Identify the functional group in compounds (i) and (iii).
parts.answer: (i) carboxylic acid group, –COOH; (iii) carbon–carbon double bond, C=C

parts.label: a
parts.text: An alkene has a relative molecular mass of 56. Deduce its molecular formula. Show your working. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
parts.answer: C₄H₈

parts.label: b
parts.text: Draw (as structural formulae) two alkenes with this molecular formula and name them.
parts.answer: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ but-1-ene; CH₃CH=CHCH₃ but-2-ene (also CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₃, methylpropene)
parts.working: B1 each correct formula with name.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The molecular formula C₃H₈O fits two alcohols. Give their structural formulae and names.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH propan-1-ol; CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ propan-2-ol

parts.label: a
parts.text: Alkanes are described as saturated hydrocarbons. Explain what saturated and hydrocarbon mean.
parts.answer: Saturated: contains only single covalent bonds (C–C). Hydrocarbon: a compound of hydrogen and carbon only.

parts.label: b
parts.text: LPG cylinders used for cooking contain propane. Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of propane, C₃H₈.
parts.answer: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O

parts.label: c
parts.text: Alkanes are generally unreactive. Give one type of reaction that they do undergo.
parts.answer: Combustion / substitution with chlorine in UV light.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Methane reacts with chlorine. State the condition needed.
parts.answer: ultraviolet (UV) light

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction that forms one organic product with one chlorine atom, and name that product.
parts.answer: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl; chloromethane

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the type of reaction and explain the name.
parts.answer: Substitution: a hydrogen atom in methane is replaced by a chlorine atom.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest the formula of the organic product formed if the reaction continues with more chlorine.
parts.answer: CH₂Cl₂ (or CHCl₃ / CCl₄)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Butane burns completely: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O. Calculate the volume of oxygen needed to burn 30 cm³ of butane, and the volume of carbon dioxide formed. (All volumes at room temperature and pressure.)
parts.answer: oxygen 195 cm³; carbon dioxide 120 cm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: In a poorly ventilated room butane burns incompletely. Name the toxic gas formed and explain why it is dangerous.
parts.answer: Carbon monoxide; it combines with haemoglobin in the blood, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which test shows that a hydrocarbon is unsaturated?
A Aqueous bromine changes from orange to colourless.
B Limewater turns milky.
C Damp red litmus paper turns blue.
D A lighted splint gives a squeaky pop.
parts.answer: A Aqueous bromine changes from orange to colourless.
parts.working: C=C bonds undergo addition with bromine, decolourising it. B tests for carbon dioxide, which forms when any hydrocarbon burns, so it does not show unsaturation.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Give the product and conditions for each reaction of ethene:
(i) with hydrogen
(ii) with steam
(iii) with bromine
parts.answer: (i) ethane; nickel catalyst, about 150 °C (ii) ethanol; phosphoric acid catalyst, about 300 °C and 6000 kPa (iii) 1,2-dibromoethane; room temperature
parts.working: (i) B1 ethane, B1 nickel catalyst + heat; (ii) B1 ethanol, B1 H₃PO₄ catalyst with high temperature and pressure; (iii) B1 1,2-dibromoethane (C₂H₄Br₂).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the type of reaction in all three cases.
parts.answer: addition

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of propene with bromine, using structural formulae, and name the product.
parts.answer: CH₃CH=CH₂ + Br₂ → CH₃CHBrCH₂Br; 1,2-dibromopropane

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the mass of bromine that reacts with 2.1 g of propene. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80)
parts.working: M1 Mr propene = 42, moles = 0.050; M1 1 : 1 ratio; A1 0.050 × 160 = 8.0 g.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why propane does not react with bromine in the dark.
parts.answer: Propane is saturated (no C=C), so it cannot undergo addition.

stem: Petroleum (crude oil) is processed at refineries such as those near Karachi.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the process used to separate petroleum into fractions and state the physical property on which it depends.
parts.answer: Fractional distillation; boiling point.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one use for each fraction: (i) refinery gas (ii) kerosene (iii) bitumen.
parts.answer: (i) fuel for heating and cooking (ii) jet fuel (iii) surfacing roads and roofs

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe how chain length and viscosity change from the top of the column to the bottom.
parts.answer: Both increase towards the bottom.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the conditions used for cracking.
parts.answer: high temperature; a catalyst

parts.label: b
parts.text: Complete the equation: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₇H₁₆ + ____. Name the product you have added.
parts.answer: C₃H₆; propene

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give two reasons why cracking is carried out.
parts.answer: Demand for shorter-chain fractions such as petrol is greater than supply; it produces alkenes for making polymers and other chemicals; it can produce hydrogen.

stem:
Percentage supply from distillation and percentage demand for petroleum fractions at one refinery:
fraction: supply %, demand %
refinery gas: 4, 8
gasoline: 11, 22
naphtha: 9, 5
kerosene: 13, 8
diesel oil: 20, 23
fuel oil and bitumen: 43, 34

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which fractions are produced in greater amounts than are needed?
parts.answer: naphtha, kerosene, fuel oil and bitumen
parts.working: 2 marks for all four; 1 mark for two or three.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the shortfall of gasoline as a percentage of the total.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how cracking helps to match supply with demand.
parts.answer: Cracking breaks long-chain molecules from surplus fractions (e.g. fuel oil) into shorter, more useful ones such as gasoline.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A long-chain alkane C₁₆H₃₄ is cracked to give one molecule of octane and ethene only. Write the balanced equation.
parts.answer: C₁₆H₃₄ → C₈H₁₈ + 4C₂H₄

author: HomiLabs

stem: Several sugar mills in Pakistan also produce ethanol from molasses.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ethanol can be made by fermentation of sugar from sugar cane molasses. State the conditions needed.
parts.answer: Yeast; temperature about 25–35 °C; absence of oxygen (anaerobic); aqueous solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the equation for the fermentation of glucose.
parts.answer: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the other industrial method of making ethanol.
parts.answer: Catalytic addition of steam to ethene (hydration of ethene).

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two uses of ethanol.
parts.answer: As a solvent; as a fuel.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of ethanol.
parts.answer: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare making ethanol by fermentation with making it by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene. Give two advantages of each method.
parts.answer: Fermentation: uses renewable raw materials (sugar crops); low temperature and normal pressure so less energy. Hydration of ethene: fast reaction; continuous process; produces pure ethanol (no need for separation); high yield.
parts.working: B1 each of two fermentation advantages; B1 each of two hydration advantages.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest why a country with a large sugar industry and little petroleum might choose fermentation.
parts.answer: Sugar (molasses) is readily available and cheap, while ethene comes from petroleum, which would have to be imported.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the maximum mass of ethanol from 90 g of glucose. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
parts.working: M1 moles glucose = 90 ÷ 180 = 0.50, moles ethanol = 1.0; A1 1.0 × 46 = 46 g.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide produced at room temperature and pressure. (Molar gas volume = 24 dm³)
parts.answer: 24 dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ethanol can be oxidised to ethanoic acid by warming with acidified aqueous potassium manganate(VII). State the colour change.
parts.answer: purple to colourless

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which ester is formed when methanol reacts with ethanoic acid?
A ethyl methanoate
B methyl ethanoate
C methyl methanoate
D ethyl ethanoate
parts.answer: B methyl ethanoate
parts.working: The alcohol gives the first part of the name (methyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). A reverses the two parts.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Vinegar contains ethanoic acid. Write a balanced equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate, and give one observation.
parts.answer: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂; effervescence (bubbles)
parts.working: B1 formulae; B1 balanced; B1 observation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the salt formed when ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium, and name the gas.
parts.answer: magnesium ethanoate; hydrogen

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid. Explain what this means.
parts.answer: It is only partially dissociated (ionised) in water.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the ester formed when ethanol reacts with propanoic acid and write its structural formula.
parts.answer: ethyl propanoate; CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the conditions for this reaction.
parts.answer: concentrated sulfuric acid (catalyst); heat (warm)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one use of esters.
parts.answer: flavourings / perfumes / solvents

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the carboxylic acid and the alcohol that react to make propyl methanoate, HCOOCH₂CH₂CH₃.
parts.answer: methanoic acid; propan-1-ol

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ethyl butanoate, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₂CH₃, has a pineapple smell. Name the acid and alcohol used to make it.
parts.answer: butanoic acid; ethanol

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the molecular formula of ethyl butanoate and calculate its relative molecular mass. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
parts.answer: C₆H₁₂O₂; 116

stem:
A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of a vinegar sample from a shop in Multan with 1.00 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide. The mean titre is 20.8 cm³.
CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of ethanoic acid in the vinegar in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 0.832 mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the concentration in g/dm³ to 3 significant figures. (Mr CH₃COOH = 60)
parts.answer: 49.9 g/dm³

parts.label: d
parts.text: Name a suitable indicator and give the colour change at the end-point.
parts.answer: Thymolphthalein: colourless to blue (accept phenolphthalein: colourless to pink).
parts.working: B1 indicator suitable for a weak acid–strong base titration (thymolphthalein or phenolphthalein; not methyl orange); B1 matching colour change at the end-point.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol.
parts.answer: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: 6.0 g of ethanoic acid reacts with excess ethanol. Calculate the maximum mass of ethyl ethanoate. (Mr: CH₃COOH = 60, CH₃COOC₂H₅ = 88)

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student obtains 5.72 g. Calculate the percentage yield.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Give two reasons why the yield is less than 100 %.
parts.answer: The reaction is reversible / reaches equilibrium; some product lost during separation or purification; some ester evaporates (volatile).

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which statement about addition polymerisation is correct?
A The polymer is the only product.
B Water is given off as each link forms.
C The monomers must contain two different functional groups.
D The monomers are saturated.
parts.answer: A The polymer is the only product.
parts.working: In addition polymerisation unsaturated monomers (C=C) join and nothing else is produced. B describes condensation polymerisation.

parts.label: a
parts.text: PVC is made from chloroethene, CH₂=CHCl. Name the type of polymerisation.
parts.answer: addition

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the repeat unit of PVC.
parts.answer: –CH₂–CHCl– (shown in brackets with continuation bonds, n outside)
parts.working: B1 single C–C backbone; B1 correct atoms and continuation bonds.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one use of PVC.
parts.answer: water pipes / insulation for electrical cables / window frames

stem: A city council plans to ban single-use plastic shopping bags.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why disposing of plastics in landfill sites causes problems.
parts.answer: Most plastics are non-biodegradable, so they remain for a very long time and take up land.
parts.working: B1 non-biodegradable; B1 persist / use up space.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe one problem caused by plastic waste in rivers and seas.
parts.answer: Harms or kills marine animals that swallow it or become trapped; microplastics enter food chains; blocks drains.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Burning plastic waste is sometimes suggested. Give one disadvantage.
parts.answer: Produces toxic gases (e.g. hydrogen chloride from PVC, carbon monoxide) / releases carbon dioxide.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest one way a city council could reduce plastic waste.
parts.answer: Ban or charge for single-use plastic bags; encourage recycling or reusable bags.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Nylon is a polyamide. Name the two types of monomer used to make it and the linkage formed.
parts.answer: a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine; amide linkage, –CONH–
parts.working: B1 dicarboxylic acid; B1 diamine; B1 amide linkage.

parts.label: b
parts.text: PET is a polyester. Name the two types of monomer and the linkage.
parts.answer: a dicarboxylic acid and a diol; ester linkage, –COO–

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the small molecule formed when each linkage is made, and the type of polymerisation.
parts.answer: water; condensation polymerisation

parts.label: a
parts.text: Proteins are natural polymers. Name the monomers and the linkage in proteins.
parts.answer: amino acids; amide (peptide) linkage

parts.label: b
parts.text: A protein chain is made from 50 amino acid molecules joined in a line. How many water molecules are eliminated?
parts.working: B1 one water molecule per linkage; 50 − 1 = 49 linkages.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one similarity and one difference between the structures of a protein and nylon.
parts.answer: Similarity: both contain amide linkages / both condensation polymers. Difference: a protein is made from many different amino acids (each monomer has both –NH₂ and –COOH groups), whereas nylon is made from two different monomers that alternate.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the repeat unit of poly(propene), made from propene CH₂=CHCH₃.
parts.answer: –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–
parts.working: B1 two-carbon backbone with continuation bonds; B1 CH₃ as a side group.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A poly(propene) molecule is made from 5000 propene molecules. Calculate its relative molecular mass. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)

parts.label: c
parts.text: The repeat unit of a non-stick coating is –CF₂–CF₂–. Give the structural formula and name of its monomer.
parts.answer: CF₂=CF₂; tetrafluoroethene
